title: A pilgrimage remembered by Dharampal
body: The historian and thinker Dharampal once described meeting a group of about twelve villagers on a train journey from Gwalior to Delhi. The group, a few women and several men, came from two villages north of Lucknow. They had been on a pilgrimage lasting three months that had taken them as far as Rameswaram in the far south, among other places. They carried bundles, earthen pots and their own food supplies such as atta, ghee and sugar. When asked whether they would stop in Delhi, they said no: they only had to change trains there, because they were going on to Haridwar, and after that they had to return home.
